questions.prompt: In the power-strip picture, what plays the role of the strip itself?
options: The heartbeat plugin, because it keeps running
The context, which does nothing until plugins are mounted on it
The config object passed to each plugin
The agent loop, because every other part depends on it
questions.explanation: The host context has no features of its own, like a power strip. Every feature, including the agent loop in the finished kernel, arrives as a plugin.

questions.prompt: You call app.plugin(heartbeat, { everyMs: 5000 }) twice with different configs. What happens?
options: The second call replaces the first heartbeat
The second call throws because the plugin is already mounted
Two independent heartbeats run, each with its own interval
Only the first call runs because plugins are deduplicated
questions.explanation: A plugin is a function run once per mount with that mount's config. Mounting it twice gives two independent copies.

questions.prompt: What problem does the heartbeat plugin expose in this first kernel?
options: Once mounted it can never be stopped, because the host does not know what it set up
It runs before the banner plugin
It needs the agent loop to exist first
questions.explanation: The interval keeps firing forever. The host only called the function and never learned how to undo what it did.
